content.text: The pulses continued until dusk. Mara traced them through the stacks, marking each place where the vibration was strongest.
Her notes formed a spiral around the central hall. At its center stood an ordinary reading desk that she had passed a dozen times before.
Beneath the desk she found a wire no thicker than thread. It vanished between the floorboards and hummed gently against her fingertip.
The brass automaton watched from the end of the aisle. When she asked where the wire led, it raised one hand and pointed upward.
There was no stair to the tower, so the ladders made one. They rolled together and locked into a steep, uncertain path toward a hatch in the darkness.
Mara climbed. The archive diminished below her until its lamps resembled a chart of distant cities. The pulses grew clearer with every rung.
Above the hatch, a small machine faced the night sky. Its dial repeated the same three marks, and its needle answered a light blinking far beyond the harbor.
Mara adjusted the machine by a single degree. The distant light became steady. Below, every sealed book in the eastern wing opened at once.
